evidence: [M] prints E(P) <= (V_j/l_m) eps^reg and E(R) <= omega^inh (rate -1/2) eps^reg for the anchored derivative sums over all addresses of T_i, plus the identity and weighted comparisons on the whole input curve; its proof treats the complementary class d_i^3 >= l_m explicitly. pressings concludes Houses ... (C'/L*incomingE) (|e s|*incomingE), whose remains field gives regularity of glyph for all i but the sup bound only under `coverNumber B.B (plate H i).support ≤ B.B → B.supBounds ... (glyph ...) (s i)`, and no continuity or difference statement along the input curve. No hypothesis in pressings or in Cash/Plays forces coverNumber <= B.B, and the downstream users (Beam.estate/shines) route the large-cover (`tired`) terms through separate Captain markPhi bounds, which confirms that [L] does not prove the remainder bound at all supports. The claim stands as weaker; it is a real scope difference, not a typo.

[M] prints E(P) <= (V_j/l_m) eps^reg and E(R) <= omega^inh eps^reg (rate -1/2) at every address of T_i, and its proof treats large supports (cover_B > B) separately to get that bound. It also claims T=P+R and weighted comparisons/continuity on the whole input curve. [L]'s pressings concludes Houses with c=C'/L*incomingE and c'=|e s|*incomingE, Rate -(1/2), but Houses.remains gives the glyph sup bound only under `coverNumber B.B (plate H i).support <= B.B -> B.supBounds ... (glyph ...) (s i)`. Beam.estate uses it only on non-`tired` addresses, where `shall` gives cover <= B, and bounds tired addresses by a separate Captain markPhi budget. Neither Houses nor BudgetPoint.Regular (locality, Borel, gauge invariance, smoothness at healthy U) states continuity in the coupling along the input curve, so the claim stands as weaker.
